You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in space group number 204, with the Hermann–Mauguin symbol Im-3 and the Hall symbol “-I 2 2 3”. The supplied input cell is not the conventional cubic cell: it is a primitive rhombohedral setting with all three lattice parameters equal to 6.42016675 angstroms and all three interaxial angles equal to 109.47122063 degrees. This cell contains 20 atoms with the declared input composition Tb1Mn4Cu3O12. All atomic positions are given as fractional coordinates, and the relation between the input and standard frames is q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P has rows (0.5, -0.5, 0.5), (0.5, 0.5, -0.5), and (-0.5, 0.5, 0.5), and the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0). Thus the standard body-centered cubic setting is recovered from the primitive input cell by this change of basis without any translational offset.

In the standard setting, the terbium sublattice occupies the twofold Wyckoff orbit 2a, represented by the point at fractional coordinates (0, 0, 0), with the coordinate relation exactly “0, 0, 0” and no free positional parameters. The manganese atoms occupy the eightfold orbit 8c, represented by (1/4, 1/4, 1/4), again with no independent coordinates beyond the fixed values one quarter along each axis. Copper is placed on the sixfold orbit 6b, represented by (0, 1/2, 1/2), corresponding to the fixed relation “0, 1/2, 1/2”. Oxygen forms the only positionally flexible sublattice: it occupies the 24-fold orbit 24g with the coordinate relation “0, y, z”, where the representative input values are y = 0.3029989999999998 and z = 0.8301660000000001. These two numbers are the sole independent positional parameters in the structure, and all other oxygen positions are generated from them by the Im-3 symmetry operations.

The numerical values are stated to six decimal places before any correction, and in this case no precision corrections are required: the listed coordinates are already the final input geometry. The complete description therefore consists of a primitive rhombohedral input cell with composition TbMn4Cu3O12, related by the specified linear transformation to the conventional Im-3 setting, in which Tb lies at the origin-type 2a site, Mn at the fixed 8c site (1/4, 1/4, 1/4), Cu at the fixed 6b site (0, 1/2, 1/2), and O at the symmetry-generated 24g sites defined by x = 0, y = 0.3029989999999998, and z = 0.8301660000000001.
